evidence_basis.originality_note: Original workshop, handwheel, control-handle and inspection-arm contexts preserve the mapped recognition, perpendicular-distance and calculation demands without copying official wording, values or diagram geometry.

questions.prompt: Define the moment of a force about a point.
Which pair of forces forms a couple?

options.A: Two parallel forces of 5 N in the same direction on separate lines
options.B: Two opposite parallel forces of 5 N on the same line of action
options.C: Two opposite parallel forces of 5 N on separate lines of action
options.D: Two opposite parallel forces of 5 N and 7 N on separate lines of action

questions.prompt: A couple consists of two forces, each of magnitude 12 N. The perpendicular distance between their lines of action is 0.25 m. What is the torque of the couple?
An unchanged couple is moved to a different position on the same rigid object. Its force magnitude and perpendicular force-line separation stay constant. What happens to its torque?

options.A: It becomes zero because the forces cancel
options.B: It decreases because the couple is farther from the centre
options.C: It increases because both forces now have larger moments
options.D: It stays the same because its torque depends on force and force-line separation

questions.prompt: A technician turns a circular handwheel using two horizontal forces. Each force has magnitude 24 N. One acts to the right at the top of the wheel and the other acts to the left at the bottom. The perpendicular distance between their lines of action is 0.34 m.

figure.purpose: Assess recognition, perpendicular separation and turning direction for a handwheel couple.
figure.brief: Landscape 3:2 pure-white black-and-white Cambridge-inspired line diagram. Show a circular handwheel, a 24 N horizontal rightward arrow tangent at the top, a 24 N horizontal leftward arrow tangent at the bottom, and a perpendicular bracket between the force lines labelled 0.34 m. Include no curved rotation arrow, formula or answer.
figure.alt_text: A handwheel has equal opposite horizontal 24 N forces at top and bottom with force lines 0.34 m apart.

parts.prompt: Explain why the two forces form a couple.

questions.prompt: A control handle is turned by a couple. The perpendicular separation of the two force lines is initially 0.18 m, and the required torque is 7.2 N m.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of each force in the couple.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The same two forces are moved so that their perpendicular separation is 0.27 m. Calculate the new torque.

questions.prompt: A horizontal inspection arm extends 0.45 m from a fixed point O to its end P. A downward force of 12 N acts at P. The arm is also acted on by a separate anticlockwise couple made by two vertical forces, each of magnitude 8.0 N, whose lines of action are 0.20 m apart.

figure.purpose: Assess a mixed prior single-force moment and current couple torque without invoking equilibrium.
figure.brief: Landscape 3:2 pure-white black-and-white Cambridge-inspired line diagram. Show a horizontal arm OP of length 0.45 m with O at the left, P at the right and a 12 N downward force at P. Separately on the arm show two vertical 8.0 N force arrows on parallel lines 0.20 m apart, arranged to give anticlockwise rotation. Include dimensions, but no curved arrows, resultant or formulas.
figure.alt_text: A horizontal arm has a 12 N downward end force and a separate pair of opposite vertical 8.0 N forces 0.20 m apart.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the moment of the 12 N force about O and state its direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the torque of the couple.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude and direction of the resultant turning effect about O.

parts.label: (d)
